summary: Wave-5 kernel blocker list all closed: (i) the 1 MiB exec gate raised to the v2 loader's 128 MiB cap (94 MB CLANG2.BIN execs in-OS, proven pre=-ENOEXEC/post=banner); (ii) fault-killed children now always reap non-zero (EC=0x00/0x3C/generic kill paths route through process_fault_set_status; t23 false rc=0 -> rc=4, unit test added); (iii) the 'housekeeping' EL1 fault (w4-clang pid=5) root-caused to the L9 prefetch kernel task racing group teardown -> vm_arch_walk deref of a dead/reused page-table chain (fault site = vm_arch_walk+0x2c, FAR 0xFFFF...F000-family) and fixed via a zero-root walk guard + an alive re-check inside the prefetch's presence-probe critical section; (iv) the L9-prefetch PROT instruction-fetch race fixed by bounded TLB-flush-and-retry in vm_handle_fault (reproduced pre-fix only: lld killed in=PROT at 0x1000673060, plus the EL1 fault + driver LOSTWAKE-disposal cascade in ONE boot; fixed kernel clean across 3 boots of the same racing script); (v) IDLESTUCK false-positives dampened by printing the table dump only when a slot was actually reclaimed/disposed (arm-only arming no longer spams; the LOSTWAKE reclaim/dispose lines still log real events); (vi) spawn/exec flat-args cap raised 255 -> 1024 kernel-side AND in crt0's argv/args copy buffers (the binding cap was the consumer; a 330-char line went from truncated argc=17 to full argc=27); (vii) MAKE.BIN recipe-shell exec triage closed as a REAL kernel bug fixed: exec of a missing image (fat16_open creates a zero-size entry) now fails cleanly pre-teardown (-ENOENT) instead of tearing down the old AS, reaching v2_map_image "bad image size 0", leaving the process AS-less and re-faulting forever (pre-fix repro shows the fault loop; fixed shows EXECX errno=2 + clean rc=1).

blockers.root_cause: process_exec_current gated EVERY exec with program_too_large() against MAX_PROGRAM_SIZE = USER_INITIAL_CLEAR_SIZE = 1 MiB (process.h:42, program_loader.c), but post-S5-flip the live exec path loads via v2_map_image whose own cap is USER_IMG_SIZE = 128 MiB.  A 126 MB CLANG.BIN / 94 MB flat CLANG2.BIN exec returned -ENOEXEC while the same image spawn+ran fine (w4-src S0/S1 blocker).
blockers.fix: Per-path exec gate: v2 exec (grp->as) checks file_size > USER_IMG_SIZE (matches the loader); the legacy v1 exec keeps the 1 MiB gate.  Also added a pre-teardown file_size==0 -> -ENOENT check (missing image; see b7).

evidence.failing: docs/selfhost/lanes/evidence-w5-kernel/prefix-i2.serial  (EXECX execv(/TOOLS/CLANG2.BIN)... EXECX exec failed errno=8 [ENOEXEC], rc=256)

blockers.root_cause: The EC=0x00 ('Unknown Reason'), EC=0x3C (BRK) and generic-vector user-fault kill paths called process_exit(tf) directly, which reaped the stale x0 left in the frame: a crash-killed tool surfaced as rc=0 -> ACCEPTANCE-COMPLETE false pass (w4-clang t23).
blockers.fix: All fault kill paths now route through process_fault_exit(tf, signo) (ARM EC=0x00/0x3C + generic; x64 generic user-exception path).  process_fault_set_status stamps PROCESS_STATUS_SIGNAL|signo into regs[0]; group_teardown maps it to the waitpid SIGNAL byte (always non-zero).  New unit test test_fault_kill_status_nonzero.

blockers.root_cause: Disassembled from the on-device serial (FAR 0xFFFF...F018, bytes@ELR, LR): the L9 prefetch kernel task (pid 5 in the desktop-mode numbering of w4-clang, pid 4 in MODE=selfhost) calls vm_arch_walk which dereferences the page-table chain to a bogus descriptor (~0xFFFF...F000 family) exactly at vm_arch_walk+0x2c (ldr x8,[x8]) while the owned process is being killed/its AS torn down.  The per-page presence probe walked the AS in a separate critical section from the batch-top alive check, so a peer CPU's group teardown could interleave and the walk touched a dead/reused table chain.  Reproduced deterministically as the cascade after the (iv) PROT kill in ONE pre-fix boot (prefix-t25b-6.serial).
blockers.fix: 1) arm mmu vm_arch_walk/x64 walk-alloc: treat root_phys==0 as absent (no deref of a dead root).  2) vm_image_prefetch_run presence probe: re-validate v2_prefetch_alive_locked in the SAME vm_lock critical section as the walk, stopping the task instead of walking a dying AS.  New unit test test_vm_walk_dead_as_safe.

evidence.failing: docs/selfhost/lanes/evidence-w5-kernel/prefix-t25b-6.serial  (FATAL EC:0x25 FAR:0xFFFFFFFFF018 ELR:...AF1AC PROC pid=4, then [LOSTWAKE] disposing pid=1 + fault thrash -> hang)
evidence.fixed: docs/selfhost/lanes/evidence-w5-kernel/fixed-t25b-2.serial  (same racing script: no FATAL, no LOSTWAKE, rc=4, clean halt; runs 1/3 likewise)

blockers.root_cause: An instruction fetch landed on an IMAGE page whose leaf became present (mapped by the background prefetch / a peer demand fill) between the hardware's translation walk and the fault handler.  vm_handle_fault's 'present but hardware said fault' branch returned 1 (PROT kill) instead of demand-filling/retrying (w4-clang t25b: pid=4 lld killed in=PROT at PC=VA=0x100064E000; reproduced pre-fix at 0x1000673060).
blockers.fix: vm_handle_fault: when the leaf is present AND permissions pass (checked before the walk), a fault is a stale-translation timing artifact -> bounded TLB flush (vm_arch_flush_va) + return 0 (trap layer eret re-executes).  Bound: FAULT_RETRY_MAX = 4 consecutive retries on the same VA, then kill.  Genuine permission violations still kill (checked earlier).

evidence.failing: docs/selfhost/lanes/evidence-w5-kernel/prefix-t25b-6.serial  (pid=3 (/TOOLS/LLD2.BIN) memory fault VA=0x1000673060 PC=0x1000673060 rw=rx in=PROT -> killed)
evidence.fixed: docs/selfhost/lanes/evidence-w5-kernel/fixed-t25b-2.serial  (3 clean boots of the same LLD2.BIN -flavor racing script: no in=PROT anytime)

blockers.item: (v) IDLESTUCK false-positives on the driver's legitimate pipe-wait
blockers.root_cause: The idle-loop 'anomaly' flag was set for a stale-claim CANDIDATE the moment it was armed (lostwake_stale_claim_reclaimable), without waiting for confirmations: on MTTCG a busy-but-live claimer's heartbeat routinely looks stale for > LOSTWAKE_DEAD_OWNER_MS, so the [IDLESTUCK] table dump spammed every ~1000 idle rounds (~1.7 s) on healthy boots and the driver's legitimate wait was named as stuck; a confirmed-stale claim could even DISPOSE the legitimately running driver (observed in the pre-fix cascade: [LOSTWAKE] disposing pid=1 SELFHOST.BIN).
blockers.fix: The [IDLESTUCK] table dump now prints only when this pass actually RECLAIMED or DISPOSED a slot (acted): mere arming of a stale-claim candidate no longer dumps.  The [LOSTWAKE] reclaim/dispose messages still name every real event, and the arm/confirm recovery logic is unchanged.

evidence.failing: docs/selfhost/lanes/evidence-w5-kernel/prefix-t25b-6.serial  ([IDLESTUCK] slot=... SELFHOST.BIN spam + [LOSTWAKE] disposing pid=1 SELFHOST.BIN (stale dead-owner claim) on a live driver)

blockers.root_cause: The flat args string is capped at 255 B in five places: sys_spawn_args pool args[256] (both trap.c), struct process.args[256], the exec-args copies, the flat[] split buffer, AND -- the binding one -- crt0's avbuf[256]/argbuf[256] argv copy buffers.  A >255-char compile line truncated mid-token (w4-clang: clang saw 'no input files').
blockers.fix: New HO_FLAT_ARGS_LEN = 1024 in process.h used for struct process.args, the spawn pool, all copy loops and the split buffer; crt0 avbuf/argbuf raised 256 -> 1024 (CRT0_AVBUF_LEN).

blockers.root_cause: fat16_open creates a ZERO-SIZE directory entry on a MISS, so exec of a missing shell/tool returned 0 with file_size==0.  process_exec_current proceeded to the v2 exec: tore down the old AS, then v2_map_image rejected 'bad image size 0' -> -ENOEXEC, leaving the process AS-less.  Its next user access faulted EC 0x20 and it re-faulted forever (the w4-src MISSING-SHELL-WEDGE 'v2 loader: bad image size 0' respawn flood; reproduced pre-fix with EXECX exec /TOOLS/NOSUCH.BIN).  The w4-src staging fix (SHELL=/TOOLS/SH.BIN staged) masks it; the kernel bug remained.
blockers.fix: process_exec_current: file_size==0 (missing image) -> clean -ENOENT BEFORE the AS teardown, so a failed exec leaves the process intact and the caller gets a real errno.  Documented residual: a failure AFTER teardown (OOM during v2_map_image/region insert) still leaves the group AS-less (pre-existing documented deviation); no minimal repro observed, left as-is.

evidence.failing: docs/selfhost/lanes/evidence-w5-kernel/prefix-vii.serial  (EXECX execv(/TOOLS/NOSUCH.BIN)... v2 loader: bad image size 0 + repeated 'User process 3 (/EXECX.BIN) fault! EC: 0x20' respawn loop)
evidence.fixed: docs/selfhost/lanes/evidence-w5-kernel/fixed-vii.serial  (EXECX execv(/TOOLS/NOSUCH.BIN)... EXECX exec failed errno=2 [ENOENT], rc=256, clean quiet halt)

files_changed: src/include/process.h (PROCESS_STATUS_SIGNAL decl process_fault_set_status; HO_FLAT_ARGS_LEN 1024; struct process.args)
src/kernel/process.c (process_fault_set_status split; IDLESTUCK dump gated on acted)
src/kernel/program_loader.c (per-path exec gate to USER_IMG_SIZE; missing-image -ENOENT pre-teardown; spawn/exec args copies + flat[] buffers)
src/kernel/vm.h + src/kernel/vm.c (AS fault-retry budget; walk-present retry/flush; prefetch presence-probe alive re-check; FAULT_RETRY_MAX)
commits: 8d14bc5 w5-kernel: fault-kill status (ii), exec gate 128MiB + missing-image pre-teardown (i/vii), prefetch fault retry (iv), IDLESTUCK dampen (v), flat args cap 1024 (vi)
137ad17 w5-kernel (iii): prefetch/AS-teardown race - walk guard + alive recheck; unit test test_vm_walk_dead_as_safe
ae6eb25 w5-kernel (vi): complete the spawn-args raise - crt0 argv/args copy buffers 256->1024
notes: Serial repros used a copy of the w4-clang probe image with a MODE=selfhost kernel swapped in; pre-fix evidence boots the base-commit (92815fa) kernel built in a scratch worktree.

The pre-fix (iv)+(iii)+(v) cascade reproduced in ONE boot (prefix-t25b-6.serial); the fixed kernel booted the identical racing script 3 times clean (fixed-t25b-{1,2,3}.serial, evidence filenames fixed-t25b-2 shown).

The toolchain-side BRK (EC 0x3C) that lld/clang hit when actually compiling is the known toolchain-build defect (w4-clang b2, toolchain-builder-owned); the kernel now reports it as rc=4 instead of a stale value.
One QEMU per tree observed; no pushes; all work committed locally on selfhost/w5-kernel.
